The inward gaze: why the women in my paintings close their eyes

November 22, 2026 · By Kimberly Marnell

If you look across my paintings, you will notice the same thing again and again. The women are rarely looking at you. Their eyes are closed or lowered, and they are somewhere inside themselves.

A private moment

I paint women in their own quiet moment, eyes closed, heart open. It is the moment just before or just after something: rest, pleasure, grief, relief. By closing the eyes, the painting stops being about being looked at and becomes about what she is feeling. You are invited in rather than confronted.

A flower as companion

A flower is often close by. In Queen of the Night a white flower sits close to her face, among botanical patterns. In Communion with the Earth, a kneeling woman leans toward a cluster of yellow flowers. The flowers are not decoration. They are a second figure in the painting, something growing alongside her.

Softness with weight

I want the work to feel tender but never sweet. Fabric, hair and smoke move; skin has real volume. In the charcoal of Timeless Monochrome Portraits that weight comes from tone alone. In Golden Hour it comes from color: pink hair and an orange skirt under a blue and golden sky, the eyes still closed.

Where it goes next

My new collection, What We Make of Free Rein, takes this idea further, toward freedom: to create, to grow and to define a life of our own making. I am releasing it one painting at a time, and collectors on my list will see each one first.
